title: Windows Settings and System Configuration
description: Explore Control Panel, Task Manager, display settings, and power options in Windows
objective: Students will explore and configure Windows settings using Control Panel and the Settings app, use Task Manager for system monitoring, and understand power management options.

steps.title: Explore the Control Panel
steps.instructions:
The Control Panel is the central place for changing system settings. Let us explore its categories.

**Open Control Panel:**
1. Press **Windows key** and type `Control Panel`
2. Press Enter
3. Make sure the view is set to **Category** (top-right dropdown)

**Explore each category (DO NOT change anything yet — just explore):**

1. **System and Security:**
   - Click on it
   - Find **System** — click it to see your computer's basic info
   - Note: Processor name, RAM, System type (32-bit or 64-bit)
   - Press the **Back** button to go back

2. **User Accounts:**
   - Click on it
   - See your account name and type (Administrator or Standard)

3. **Hardware and Sound:**
   - Click on it
   - Find **Devices and Printers** — see what devices are connected
   - Find **Power Options** — see the current power plan

4. **Programs:**
   - Click **Programs and Features**
   - This shows ALL installed programs on your computer
   - Note: How many programs are installed? ___________
   - DO NOT uninstall anything!

5. **Clock and Region:**
   - Click on it
   - Check the date format and time zone
   - India should show: IST (UTC+05:30)

**Fill this table:**

| Setting | Value on Your Computer |
|---------|------------------------|
| Processor | ___________ |
| RAM | ___________ |
| System Type | ___________ |
| Account Type | ___________ |
| Current Power Plan | ___________ |
| Number of Installed Programs | ___________ |
| Time Zone | ___________ |

**CCC Exam Connection:** Control Panel is the traditional settings manager in Windows. Know its main categories.

steps.title: Customize Display Settings
steps.instructions:
Let us practice changing how your computer screen looks.

**Part A — Screen Resolution:**
1. Right-click on the Desktop
2. Click **Display settings**
3. Scroll to **Display resolution**
4. Note your current resolution: ___________
5. Click the dropdown to see other available resolutions
6. **DO NOT change the resolution** — just note what options are available
7. The recommended resolution is usually the highest one listed

**Part B — Change Desktop Wallpaper:**
1. Right-click on the Desktop > **Personalize**
2. Click **Background**
3. Under "Choose your background", select **Picture**
4. Click **Browse photos** and select any image from your computer
   - Or choose one of the default Windows wallpapers
5. See how the wallpaper changes
6. Try changing "Choose a fit" to:
   - **Fill** — fills the screen, may crop edges
   - **Fit** — fits the image, may show bars on sides
   - **Stretch** — stretches to fill (may distort)
   - **Center** — places image in the center
7. After experimenting, set it back to the original if needed

**Part C — Change Theme Colours:**
1. In Personalization, click **Colors**
2. Note the current accent colour
3. Try selecting a different colour from the palette
4. Toggle "Show accent colour on Start and taskbar" — see the effect
5. Change it back to your preference

**Part D — Screen Saver:**
1. In the search box of Personalization, type **Screen saver**
2. Or go to Lock Screen > Screen saver settings
3. Choose a screen saver from the dropdown (e.g., Bubbles, Mystify)
4. Click **Preview** to see how it looks
5. Set the wait time to **5 minutes**
6. Click OK

**CCC Exam Connection:** Right-click Desktop > Display settings is how you access screen resolution. Right-click Desktop > Personalize is for wallpaper.

steps.title: Use Task Manager
steps.instructions:
Task Manager is an essential tool for monitoring and troubleshooting. Let us explore it in detail.

**Open Task Manager:**
- Press **Ctrl + Shift + Esc** (this is the fastest method)
- If it opens in simple mode, click **More details** at the bottom

**Explore the Processes Tab:**
1. This shows all running programs and background processes
2. Click the **CPU** column header to sort by CPU usage (highest first)
3. Note: Which app is using the most CPU? ___________
4. Click the **Memory** column header to sort by memory usage
5. Note: Which app is using the most RAM? ___________
6. Note: How many background processes are running? ___________

**Explore the Performance Tab:**
1. Click the **Performance** tab
2. **CPU section:**
   - Current utilization: ___________
   - Speed (clock speed): ___________
   - Cores: ___________
   - Up time: ___________
3. **Memory section:**
   - In use: ___________ GB out of ___________ GB
   - Available: ___________ GB
4. **Disk section:**
   - Is it HDD or SSD? (SSD usually shows 0% when idle)

**Explore the Startup Tab:**
1. Click the **Startup** tab
2. This shows programs that automatically start when Windows boots
3. Count:
   - Total startup items: ___________
   - Enabled: ___________
   - Disabled: ___________
4. Look at the **Startup Impact** column — programs with "High" impact slow down your boot time
5. **To disable a startup program:** Right-click > Disable
   - Only disable programs you recognize and don't need at startup
   - NEVER disable antivirus or system services!

**Practice ending a task:**
1. Open **Notepad** (so we have something safe to end)
2. Go back to Task Manager > Processes tab
3. Find **Notepad** in the list
4. Right-click on it > **End task**
5. Notepad closes immediately

**CCC Exam Connection:** Ctrl + Shift + Esc opens Task Manager directly. Ctrl + Alt + Delete opens a security screen where Task Manager is one option.

steps.title: Configure Power and Sound Settings
steps.instructions:
Let us explore power management and sound settings.

**Part A — Power Options:**
1. Open Control Panel > Hardware and Sound > **Power Options**
   (Or search for "Power" in Settings)
2. See the available power plans:
   - **Balanced** (recommended) — good balance of performance and energy
   - **Power Saver** — saves battery, reduces performance
   - **High Performance** — maximum performance, uses more power
3. Note your current plan: ___________
4. Click **Change plan settings** next to your current plan
5. See the settings for:
   - Turn off display after: ___________ minutes
   - Put computer to sleep after: ___________ minutes
6. Click **Cancel** (don't change anything)

**Part B — Understand Power Options:**
Test these power actions (your trainer will guide you):

| Action | How to Do It | What Happens |
|--------|-------------|-------------|
| Lock | Press **Windows + L** | Screen locks, need password to unlock |
| Sleep | Start > Power > Sleep | Low power, quick wake up |
| Restart | Start > Power > Restart | Shuts down and starts again |

**DO NOT shut down or hibernate during the lab session!**

**Part C — Sound Settings:**
1. Click the **Volume icon** in the system tray (bottom-right)
2. Note the current volume level: ___________
3. Drag the slider to change volume — notice the change
4. Click the **speaker icon** next to the slider to mute
5. Click it again to unmute
6. Right-click the Volume icon > **Sound settings**
7. Check:
   - Output device: ___________ (speakers or headphones)
   - Input device: ___________ (microphone)

**Part D — Mouse Settings:**
1. Open Settings > Devices > Mouse
   (Or Control Panel > Hardware and Sound > Mouse)
2. Note: Is the primary button Left or Right? ___________
3. Try changing the cursor speed — move the slider
4. Notice how the mouse moves faster or slower
5. Set it back to a comfortable speed

**CCC Exam Connection:** Sleep keeps RAM powered (quick wake). Hibernate saves to disk (no power, slower wake). Windows + L locks the screen.

steps.title: Run System Tools and Review
steps.instructions:
Let us use a few more system tools and then review everything.

**Part A — Run Dialog:**
1. Press **Windows + R** to open the Run dialog
2. Try these commands one at a time:
   - Type `notepad` > OK — opens Notepad
   - Type `calc` > OK — opens Calculator
   - Type `mspaint` > OK — opens Paint
   - Type `control` > OK — opens Control Panel
   - Type `msinfo32` > OK — opens System Information
3. Close all opened windows

**Part B — System Information:**
1. Press Windows + R > type `msinfo32` > OK
2. Note down:
   - OS Name: ___________
   - System Type: ___________
   - Processor: ___________
   - Total Physical Memory: ___________
   - BIOS Version: ___________

**Part C — Command Prompt (CLI):**
1. Press Windows key > type `cmd` > press Enter
2. The Command Prompt opens — this is the CLI (Command Line Interface)
3. Type these commands (press Enter after each):
   - `date /t` — shows today's date
   - `time /t` — shows current time
   - `hostname` — shows computer name
   - `dir` — lists files in current directory
   - `ver` — shows Windows version
4. Type `exit` to close Command Prompt

**Part D — Final Review Quiz:**
Answer these questions on paper or in Notepad:

1. What keyboard shortcut opens File Explorer? ___________
2. What shortcut opens Task Manager directly? ___________
3. What does Shift + Delete do? ___________
4. What is the difference between Sleep and Hibernate? ___________
5. What does Windows + L do? ___________
6. Name 3 categories in Control Panel: ___________
7. What is the file extension for an executable program? ___________
8. What is the Run dialog shortcut? ___________
9. What does F2 do when a file is selected? ___________
10. Is Linux open source or proprietary? ___________

**Answers:** 1) Win+E, 2) Ctrl+Shift+Esc, 3) Permanently deletes, 4) Sleep=RAM powered/Hibernate=saved to disk, 5) Locks screen, 6) Any 3 from notes, 7) .exe, 8) Win+R, 9) Rename, 10) Open source

**Submit your completed answers and observations to your trainer.**
